description.narrative:
Detta är den sjätte fasen av stöd sedan 2010, som syftar till att konsolidera och institutionalisera tidigare resultat.
Under denna fas kommer projektet att fokusera på följande centrala handlingslinjer: 1) Kapacitetsutveckling och lagstiftningsstöd, 2) Främjande av medborgarnas deltagande och det civila samhällets engagemang, 3) Främjande av utbildning och expertis inom säkerhetssektorn, och 4) Främjande av jämställdhetsintegrering i säkerhetssektorn.
Det kommer även fortsättningsvis att vara ett mångfacetterat projekt med många intressenter från både statlig och icke-statlig sektor. Nyckelpartnerna inkluderar inrikesministeriets sektor för krishantering, Belgrads universitet (fakulteten för statsvetenskap och fakulteten för säkerhetsstudier), kommissionär för information av allmän betydelse och skydd av personuppgifter, försvarsministeriet, civilsamhället, akademin och media . Ledarskapet kommer att ligga i händerna på OSSE, som kommer att fungera som en samordnare. Individuellt ledarskap och enskilda projektpartners engagemang kommer dock att vårdas genom gemensamt beslutsfattande.

This is the sixth phase of support since 2010, aiming at consolidating and institutionalizing previous results.
During this phase, the project will focus on the following key lines of action: 1) Capacity development and legislative support, 2) Promotion of citizens' participation and civil society engagement, 3) Advancing education and expertise in the security sector, and 4) Promoting gender mainstreaming in the security sector. It will continue to be a multifaceted project with many stakeholders from both the government and non-governmental sector. The key partners include the Ministry of Interior's Sector for Emergency Management, University of Belgrade (Faculty of Political Science and Faculty of Security Studies), Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection, Ministry of Defence, civil society, academia, and media. Leadership will be in the hands of the OSCE, who will act as a coordinator. However, individual leadership and the commitment of individual project partners will be nurtured through joint decision-making.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sweden, represented by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, represented by the OSCE Mission to Serbia, regarding the programme "Consolidating the Democratization Process in the Security Sector in Serbia – Phase 6"
Beslut om Insats OSSE DEMOKRATISK TILLSYN I SERBIEN 2024-2027

description.narrative:
The initial twelve-month period of the project has focused on building a solid foundation across all priority areas, despite a challenging socio-political environment.
Result 1 (personal data protection): The process of amending Serbia's Law on Personal Data Protection commenced in January 2025, with a focus on artificial intelligence and clearer data processing regimes. A tailored study visit to Austria for 15 representatives from the Office of the Commissioner's and the Ministry of Interior was organized to exchange comparative practices on data protection in digital and law enforcement contexts. The second data protection national awareness campaign was launched, with a central component of developing a series of short animated videos containing relevant information for citizens. The OSCE Mission's assessment is that technical cooperation with the Commissioner's office has deepened, despite withdrawal of civil society from government bodies;
Result 2 (emergency management): Two district-level emergency simulation exercises were successfully conducted in Jablanica (May 2025) and Pomoravlje (October 2025), involving 203 participants. Guide "Inclusive Response in Emergencies: A Guide for Firefighting and Rescue Units" was developed to address the specific needs of persons with disabilities and printed in 2,000 copies. Out of these, 1,960 were distributed to the Ministry of Interior's Sector for Emergency Management, Department for Firefighting and rescue units, for further dissemination to members of firefighting and rescue units across Serbia. A clear demand for additional simulation exercises became apparent, particularly to further support non-professional members of emergency headquarters in fully understanding operational workflows and decision making processes. Finally, English language training for MoI Sector for Emergency Management continued.
Result 3 (civil society): Despite a deterioration in CSO-government relations, a public Call for Proposals was published, resulting in the selection and contracting of eight CSO-led projects. These initiatives address critical issues such as community safety, digital rights, and gun policy reform. Furthermore, the Civil Society Network 1325 prepared its monitoring plan for the newly adopted third National Action Plan (NAP) on UNSCR 1325 (Women, Peace and Security). The Mission has noted strong youth engagement and demand for digital rights and community safety initiatives.
Result 4 (education): A new scholarship cycle was launched, resulting in the selection of 13 recipients (7 MA and 6 PhD) to pursue security-related studies at civilian faculties. Support continued for the Regional Security Knowledge Hub (RSKH), now in its third phase, which has enhanced its academic content and visibility.
